findings.title: Returning null from getSubGroupsCount() may cause NPE at call sites
findings.body: When the group is deleted concurrently, `modelSupplier.get()` returns null and this method returns `null`. The caller `GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount` passes the result to `representation.setSubGroupCount(group.getSubGroupsCount())`. If `setSubGroupCount` takes a primitive `long`, this will NPE on unboxing. Even if it takes `Long`, downstream code that unboxes will fail. The rest of this class throws `IllegalStateException` when the model is not found (see `getDelegateForUpdate()` line 61 and `isUpdated()` line 74), so this is inconsistent with the established error-handling pattern.

findings.title: Same NPE risk exists in other methods using modelSupplier.get() without null check
findings.body: The fix only guards `getSubGroupsCount()`, but `getSubGroupsStream(String, Integer, Integer)` (line 256), `getSubGroupsStream(Integer, Integer)` (line 261), and `getSubGroupsStream(String, Boolean, Integer, Integer)` (line 268) all call `modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...)` without a null check. Under the same concurrent-deletion scenario that this PR addresses, these methods will still throw an NPE. The fix is incomplete.

findings.title: Test has a race condition: reader thread may never execute during deletion window
findings.body: The reader thread is started and then groups are immediately deleted. There is no synchronization (e.g., a CountDownLatch or similar) to guarantee the reader thread has actually begun executing `groups()` calls before deletions start. On a fast machine or under thread-scheduling pressure, all 100 deletions could complete before the reader thread gets its first iteration, making the test pass vacuously without ever exercising the concurrent path it intends to test.

findings.title: No join() on reader thread; assertion may run before thread completes
findings.body: After setting `deletedAll.set(true)`, the test immediately asserts on `caughtExceptions`. The reader thread may still be in-flight (between the `while` condition check and the `groups()` call) when the assertion runs. Although unlikely to cause a false pass (the thread would need to throw after the assertion), a `thread.join()` before the assertion would make the test deterministic and correct.

findings.title: Test does not register cleanup for created groups
findings.body: Other tests in this class use `managedRealm.cleanup().add(...)` to ensure resources are removed after the test. This test creates 100 groups and deletes them inline, but if the test fails during creation (e.g., at group 50), the already-created groups are left behind and may interfere with subsequent tests or leave the realm in a dirty state.
